stories.headline: Satyendar Jain, Delhi Jal Board ex-CEO among 6 arrested for 'scam'
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Nearly two years after 
Satyendar Jain
, former minister in erstwhile AAP govt, was released on bail from Tihar Jail in an alleged ED money laundering case filed, Delhi govt's Anti-Corruption Branch Tuesday arrested him, along with 
Delhi Jal Board
 ex-CEO Udit Prakash Rai and four others in an alleged DJB scam.
Jain had spent nearly one-and-a-half years in incarceration after being arrested in the money laundering case on May 31, 2022. He was granted bail on Oct 18, 2024.
According to joint commissioner of police Vikramjit Singh, the case stems from a formal complaint filed by the directorate of vigilance which alleges widespread irregularities, manipulation of tender criteria and illicit collusion in the tendering process for the augmentation and upgradation of DJB's sewage treatment plants.
 Tendering criteria tailored to stifle competition: ACB
The other four individuals taken into custody are former DJB contractual consultant Ankit Srivastava, AN Enterprises proprietor Nagendra Yadav, Euroteck Environment owner Raja Kumar Kurra and Srijanhar proprietor Pankaj Verma.
ACB investigations claimed to have revealed that the tendering criteria were heavily tailored to mandate restrictive technical specifications that favored Euroteck Environment, “thereby stifling fair competition”.
“Essential effluent parameters were omitted, a mandatory pilot study was bypassed and sudden technical specification changes were inserted to deliver significant, unfair financial benefits to the private entity at a steep cost to the public exchequer,” ACB alleged.
Electronic evidence seized during the probe uncovered active communications between the private operators and govt officials, showing that draft corrigenda and restrictive terms were routinely shared before being officially integrated into DJB tender notices, it added.
Financial tracing uncovered a complex money-trail designed to disguise kickbacks as commercial transactions through intermediary entities, specifically Srijanhar and AN Enterprises, the agency alleged.
ACB claimed to have established that Udit Prakash Rai, as then DJB CEO, received bribes of Rs 1.5 crore through banking channels via Nagendra Yadav’s firm, AN Enterprises, with the initial funds originating from Euroteck.

ACB officials said further investigation into the broader nexus and money trail was on. ED had earlier shared its probe report with the vigilance directorate. It claimed to have found irregularities in the award of tenders for upgradation and augmentation of at least 10 STPs for more than Rs 1,900 crore.

stories.headline: In aatmanirbharta push, 405 defence items to be indigenised
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Rajnath Singh-led defence ministry has notified sixth positive indigenisation list (PIL) comprising 405 strategically important items with an estimated business potential of Rs 3,070 crore, a move that seeks to reduce dependence on imports and give a further push to ‘atmanirbharta’ in defence production.
The list contains line replaceable units, sub-systems, sub-assemblies, spares, components and raw materials linked to key military platforms such as advanced and light utility helicopters, Su-30MKI and LCA (Tejas), armoured platforms like T-72, T-90 tanks and BMP-II, warships and missile systems.
Notified by the department of defence production (DDP), the list includes 16 items of Indian Coast Guard (ICG) and 389 items of defence public sector undertakings (DPSU). PIL is Modi govt’s policy tool that bans the import of specific military equipment, platforms and spare parts after set deadlines. It forces the military to buy these designated items only from local Indian manufacturers to boost self-reliance.
The list also covers items for missile systems such as Konkurs-M, Invar and MRSAM; electronics, including radars, sonars, fire control systems and satellite communication systems; high-explosive anti-tank ammunition and other critical defence equipment.
Upon successful indigenous development, these items will be procured from the Indian industry. DPSUs and ICG will undertake indigenisation through various routes, including their ‘make’ procedure and in-house development, with participation from the industry, particularly MSMEs.
DDP launched Sarijan defence portal in Aug 2020 as a dedicated platform through which DPSUs and Service Headquarters (SHQs) offer defence items to the industry, including MSMEs and start-ups, for indigenous development and production.
Since its launch, the portal has facilitated the offer of more than 33,000 defence items for indigenisation by DPSUs and SHQs up to June 2026. These include 5,012 items notified under the first five PILs. More than 15,700 defence items have been successfully indigenised, resulting in an estimated import substitution value of about Rs 9,000 crore over the last five years. In addition, DPSUs have placed procurement orders, including in-house production, worth Rs 10,000 crore on domestic vendors up to March 2026.

stories.headline: Census 2027 questionnaire seeks parents’ religion, place of birth up to village level
stories.deck: Besides the open field option to declare caste, respondents can choose “Does not want to declare Caste” and “No Caste”
stories.bodyText:
The questionnaire or the schedule for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027, which has gone live in Ladakh and snow-bound areas of three other States ahead of the rest of the country, seeks information on religion, date of birth and place of birth up to the village level of both the father and mother, according to the questions seen by The Hindu.
Under the data head “Family Particulars,” the questionnaire also has an option to record the place of birth of the father and mother if they were born outside India. Other than the six religions—Hindu, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Muslim and Jain—respondents can record “other religion” in a separate column.
Caste enumeration
Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe respondents can choose their caste from a predetermined drop-down menu, while all others will have to type the caste name in an open field. This is Independent India’s first caste enumeration. Question 10 (C) says: “If not SC/ST in this State/UT-Enter Caste name.” There are two other options besides the caste field: “Does not want to declare Caste” and “No Caste.” The data fields are marked “mandatory.”
Only the Union Government can issue the SC/ST list after being ratified by Parliament.
New questions
The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI) on August 14 notified a set of 40 questions to be asked during the population enumeration phase, or the second phase of the Census, adding 13 new questions or data fields that were not part of the Census 2011 questionnaire., which had 29 questions.
The questions added for the first time include spouse’s name, nationality, father’s particulars and mother’s particulars, digital literacy, permanent residential address, place of COVID-19 vaccination, number of bank accounts, passport number, driving licence availability and mobile, Aadhaar and voter ID numbers, if available.
NPR overlap
Some of the additional questions, such as particulars of mother and father, Aadhaar, mobile, voter ID and driving license details, mirror those asked in the rehearsal form for the National Population Register (NPR) in 2019. The NPR, which was initially proposed to be updated with the first phase of the Census, has been put on the back burner amid opposition from political parties and civil society members, over concerns that the data can be used to create a countrywide National Register of Citizens (NRC).
The NPR, first prepared in 2011 and updated in 2015, already has a family-wise database of 119 crore residents.
Unlike Census data, which can only be released in an aggregate form up to the village level, the NPR database can be shared with States and other government departments.
The Census schedule, which was made available to respondents in Ladakh, parts of Jammu and Kashmir, Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh on August 17 through a self-enumeration portal, ahead of the rest of the country, further expands the data fields notified in the Gazette of India.
Door-to-door enumeration
Door-to-door enumeration in these States will begin on September 1, and conclude on September 30. In the rest of the country, the second phase will be conducted in February 2027.
The question on the place of COVID-19 vaccination gives two options—within India or outside India. The names of the State and district where the vaccination was administered are to be provided if the jab was taken in India.
The open-field methodology to record caste has been questioned by the Congress. On Tuesday, Congress leader Jairam Ramesh, in a post on X, accused the government of sabotaging the caste Census. “The conclusion is clear: the Modi Govt wants to simply sabotage the caste census. The PM had made a complete U-turn on April 30, 2025 and announced that a caste census - which he had earlier attacked as an “urban naxal” idea - would take place. Now he has done another U-turn on his earlier U-turn and without saying so has buried the idea of a caste census. He is an U-turn ustad,” Mr. Ramesh said.
He said that on September 21, 2021, the Union Government had filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court categorically rejecting the plea for a caste census.
“However, Para 12 (d) in the affidavit says the following: ‘There was no registry of caste prepared prior to the conduct of 2011 Census. It would have been ideal for the Registry of Castes that there should have been given a drop-down menu for selection of the castes which could have made some consistent data available which can be relied upon.' The question now is this: why does Census 2027 NOT have this drop-down menu that the Modi Government recommended in the affidavit it submitted to the Supreme Court in Sept 2021? Such a menu had, in fact, been prepared prior to the caste surveys both in Bihar and Telangana. Such a menu had also been suggested by the Congress President in his letter to the PM of May 5, 2025,” he said.
The open-field method had resulted in the 2011 Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) returning over 46 lakh different “caste names”, largely owing to the differences in what people understood by caste. Significantly, the government has consistently maintained over the last decade that the 2011 SECC’s caste data were unreliable because of “errors” in data collection.
The total number of castes recorded during the 1931 Census was 4,147. The SECC was conducted as a survey outside the purview of the Census Act, 1948 and had no statutory backing. The data have never been released by the government.

stories.headline: Tired of swiping? Bengaluru’s singles are going offline to find a connection
stories.bodyText:
For a generation that grew up swiping right and left, meeting someone across a table might sound old-fashioned. Yet speed-dating events are finding a new audience in Bengaluru, where young professionals are looking beyond dating apps to meet people face-to-face and see where the evening takes them.
For 28-year-old banking professional and storyteller Sudhanshu, who has attended speed-dating events, the appeal lies in meeting people without the pressure of defining the outcome. “I feel when you meet someone, it’s not always about finding out what you want in life. Sometimes you learn what you don’t want in life,” he says.
Unlike dating apps, where conversations can stretch for days before two people actually meet, speed dating puts people in the same room and gives them a limited window to connect. Games and activities are often used to make first conversations less awkward. “You get to know multiple people in two hours. There are games and even blindfolded conversations. That way, you get to know the real person,” says Sudhanshu. Riya, an IT professional who has attended a speed-dating event, points out how the format offers a break from the predictability of dating apps. “On a dating app, you can spend so much time deciding whether to swipe right. 
Here, you just meet the person and see if you click. It feels more spontaneous,” she says.
Sudhanshu believes the format works because it does not necessarily come with a fixed end goal. “You don’t always go on a date with finding a partner as the only end goal. Sometimes, you meet someone just to get to know each other. Later, it can become a relationship, a marriage or a partnership,” he says.
For young professionals in a city where work schedules and busy social lives can make organic connections difficult, such events also offer a structured way to meet strangers. “Bengaluru has a lot of people who are new to the city or are busy with work. An event gives you an excuse to actually step out and talk to people,” says Riya. Sudhanshu, who recently moved to Bengaluru from Delhi, agrees. “Events like this really help us socialise with many people because someone is there to lead the activity. You get to know different perspectives and become more empathetic,” he shares.

stories.headline: Bengaluru’s 15-lakh sapling Guinness bid cost Rs 12.5 crore
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Bangalore Development Authority’s ambitious bid to set a Guinness World Record by planting 15 lakh saplings in June came with a hefty price tag of Rs 12.5 crore.
Responding to a question from Yelahanka BJP MLA SR Vishwanath in the legislative assembly Tuesday, CM 
DK Shivakumar
 said BDA spent that amount on the record attempt, including procurement and transportation of saplings, hiring Guinness World Record consultants, digital platform charges and advertisements.
The BDA procured three broad categories of planting material for the drive. Around 5 lakh saplings of common native tree species were purchased at Rs 54.7 each, while 3 lakh shrubs and medicinal plants were procured at Rs 45 per sapling. The remaining 7.5 lakh saplings comprised rare, endangered and threatened species. Besides, the authority onboarded 23 NGOs to maintain the saplings after planting to ensure survival and upkeep of the plantation.
BDA sourced the 15 lakh saplings, covering 350 species, from two vendors. Ishan Native Plants of Kondashettihalli near Hesaraghatta supplied 10.5 lakh saplings, while Shivanna of Makali in Channapatna taluk of Ramanagara district supplied another 5 lakh.
The record attempt was spread across nearly 200 acres at three locations. As many as 8,29,251 saplings were planted across 103.6 acres in Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Layout and Banashankari 6th Stage. The remaining 7,31,350 saplings were planted across 94.7 acres in Dr Shivaram Karanth Layout, Yelahanka.

stories.headline: JD(S) demands Karnataka govt. drop Bidadi Township Project
stories.deck: The party hit back at the Chief Minister, who has been arguing that both the Bidadi Township Project and the NICE Road were initiated by JD(S) governments
stories.bodyText:
Janata Dal (Secular) supremo and former Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda demanded that the Karnataka government drop the Bidadi Township project, arguing that it would deprive a large number of small farmers of their livelihoods.
He was speaking at a rally at Freedom Park on Tuesday, held as the culmination of the padayatra led by the party’s Youth Wing president Nikhil Kumaraswamy against the project.
Mr. Gowda pointed out that farmers owning even a few guntas of land, as well as those engaged in dairy farming, would be severely affected by the project. He stressed that public hearings conducted by former Justices Santosh Hegde and V. Gopala Gowda had recommended dropping the project after assessing the ground realities, but the government was not willing to heed their advice. Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders, upset over the JD(S) announcing the padayatra on its own and later joining its launch, were conspicuous by their absence at Tuesday’s event.
Mr. Gowda, Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy and Mr. Nikhil hit back at the Congress and Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, who have been pointing out that both the Bidadi Township and NICE Road projects were initiated by JD(S) governments. They argued that several changes had subsequently been made to these projects by successive Congress governments. The Karnataka Congress had termed the two projects the “Siamese twins” of the JD(S).
“Yes, I had considered the proposal for the Bidadi township, but it remained only a proposal and did not even reach the stage of a preliminary notification. As recorded in the Vidhana Sabha proceedings, I had openly stated that I would not go against the farmers and dropped it in full public view,” Mr. Kumaraswamy said, questioning why the Congress, which had opposed the project then, was championing it now. Mr. Nikhil said it was Mr. Shivakumar who had given the project a new lease of life in 2023 by holding meetings and subsequently issuing preliminary and final notifications.
NICE Road
Responding to Mr. Kumaraswamy’s demand that the government take over the NICE Road project and stop the collection of toll following the recent observations of the High Court of Karnataka, Mr. Shivakumar had hit back, arguing that it was the JD(S) that had initiated the project.
Mr. Gowda pointed out that although he had signed the MoU in 1995, the terms and conditions were subsequently revised and the course of the project was altered by successive governments.
“The clause in the MoU stated that NICE could collect toll only after constructing the Bengaluru-Mysuru Road and developing five townships. This was never done, and I have been fighting against this for years,” he said.
Mr. Kumaraswamy alleged that it was Mr. Shivakumar, who chaired the Bengaluru-Mysuru Infrastructure Corridor project in 1999 as the State’s Urban Development Minister, who had granted several permissions to NICE.
He again challenged the Chief Minister to participate in an open debate on the two projects. “I will set the stage. You can bring all your 136 MLAs,” he said. Responding to a similar challenge earlier, Mr. Shivakumar had asked the Union Minister to meet him in the Vidhana Soudha, to which Mr. Kumaraswamy said the debate should happen in Bidadi, a request that the Chief Minister did not accept.

stories.headline: Going above and beyond with Liminal
stories.deck: Liminal will showcase the works of seven artists from Karnataka at the MKF Museum of Art
stories.bodyText:
“I wanted to bring various voices together in a celebration of freedom. I believe art is the freedom of expression, and emotion,” says Belinda Fernandez of ARTELLA, curator of the show, Liminal. “It felt apt considering this is the month we celebrate our Independence as a nation.”
According to Belinda, the exhibition distills the essence of human journeys as experienced by each artist.
“Each of their styles is uniquely different; you will not see an overlap of art or thought in their work. Each of them have their own signature when it comes to representing their emotions through art,” says Belinda, who admits since seven is her favourite number, she chose as many artists for the show.
Participating artists include Bharath Laddiyavar, Gangadhar Bandanavar, Ramesh Garawad, Santosh Pattar, Shrishail Kamate, Shweta Hegde and Sumukhraj N. All the artists hail from different regions of Karnataka and between them have works executed using oil pastels, charcoal, acrylic, water colours and more.
Belinda says Gangadhar Laddiyavar has a way of presenting mythology in a contemporary manner that will appeal to today’s generation. "He wants to tell a story; he does not want us to forget our traditions, culture or the past of things,” she says.
Bharat’s use of flora to express human emotions, “resonates with us Bangaloreans who take pride in our garden city. And the wee bit of nudity found in his work, is quite tastefully done.”
On the other hand, Shrishail Kamate’s work is a stark reminder of the degradation of our environment. He shows the city from an aerial point of view; a perspective that not only makes it hard to ignore green patches giving way to growing greys and browns, but also evokes a sense of nostalgia.
Santosh Pattar draws inspiration from folk art and his rural roots. “For him, it is all about nature, the environment, and human connectivity as he believes all three need to always blend in for a harmonious existence. Santosh’s art brings to the fore our farmers and their importance in our lives. He brings in an emotional connect, telling us a story about that as well.”
Ramesh Garawad has an inclination for human faces and their story, says Belinda. “He also loves tradition and his work depicts the kind of clothes we used to wear, how our society carried itself. The eyes of his subjects are their most important feature, exuding a peace and calm that is rare in today’s world.”
Shweta Hegde uses art as therapy, and looks at life from a perspective of beauty. As a result, her works whether they are of a landscape or just flowers can be therapeutic, bringing in a different emotional connect.
Since Sumukhraj N uses charcoal, each of his works take longer to complete, and each piece invites contemplation. Belinda says, “I chose the name Liminal since it is a threshold for different emotions of seven people with seven different perspectives.”
Liminal will go on display at MKF Museum of Art from August 22 to September 2. Entry free, Mondays closed.

briefs.headline: 12-year-old files police complaint against neighbour abusing mom in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: A 12-year-old boy drew public attention by writing down a complaint copy on behalf of his mother at Nelamangala Town police station Monday.
Accepting the complaint made against a neighbour for hurling abuses at his mother, cops registered a non-cognisable report case, summoned the neighbour and took an undertaking from him not to repeat the act.
In his complaint, the boy requested police to direct the man not to harass his mother any more. A govt school student, the boy came to the station with his mother and younger sister after the neighbour, allegedly in an inebriated condition, abused the mother.
Hurt by the abuse, the mother asked the boy to accompany her to the station so that they could lodge a complaint.

briefs.headline: Parking overhaul at K.R. Market brings seamless movement but hits small vendors’ businesses
briefs.deck: The Greater Bengaluru Authority has installed barricades and created a dedicated route to enter the facility, halving the width of Avenue Road for the purpose
briefs.bodyText:
Entering K.R. Market was itself a herculean task, but not anymore. For the past three months, since the parking infrastructure was revamped and developed into a first-of-its-kind smart parking facility in the city, visitors have had a clear way to enter the parking facility.
The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has installed barricades and created a dedicated route to enter the facility, halving the width of Avenue Road for the purpose. Now, visitors do not have to endure prolonged queues and traffic at the starting point itself to enter the parking lot.
However, for small vendors outside the market, their business has not been the same. The merchants’ association has reported a reduced footfall amid the parking arrangements and the ongoing infrastructure projects around the place.
Cramped up, dip in business
Asha, a flower vendor who sits just outside the parking lot, explained that the steel barricades installed to make way for vehicles make it feel as though they are placed behind bars, trying to sell their products while visitors ignore them.
“All the vendors who used to do business on the Avenue Road have been moved behind the barricades. The whole stretch is cramped up with very little space to even sit,” she said.
Radha, who has been selling flowers outside the market for the last 20 years, explained the buyer behaviour shaped by the barricading, which has reportedly affected their businesses.
“Earlier, the visitors would stop at the starting point, buy a few items, and then enter the main market to buy bigger items. Now that the barricades are installed, most visitors directly enter the parking area and from there head inside the market,” she explained.
Lost customers?
G.M. Divakar, president, K.R. Market Flowers Merchants’ Association, reiterated that there had been a fall in footfall, explaining, “The parking was closed for many months, which had already caused traditional buyers to explore other options. In addition, now the parking system is in place with a slightly expensive fee, which has also affected the footfall.”
He noted that even for employees of shops in the building, the paid parking is pinching their pockets, as they are spending around ₹2,000 more every month.
Mr. Divakar also noted that the recent demolition of 180 shops opposite the market, as part of the footpath clearance, is likely to affect businesses further.
Santhosha Chandrashekar, a fruit vendor, added that those cleared shops had been operating for more than three decades and had frequent customers, who may stop coming now. “This market is known as a one-stop store for people to buy various items. As of now more than 180 shops have been cleared, several items won’t be available for visitors, which could alter the footfall,” he said.
“Several middle-class and lower-class people visit the market, and for them, parking charges will be an extra expense,” he added.
In the meantime, more than four stretches around the market have been taken up for civic works, leading to jam-packed roads. Such congestion across the market, according to the vendors, has also added to the reasons for reduced footfall.
GBA defends move
A senior engineer in charge of the market told The Hindu that the barricading arrangement is deliberate to ensure seamless movement of vehicles so that the parking is organised. “Initially, it may appear to cause a fall in footfall, but when a system is in place, more buyers will visit and footfall will rise,” he explained.
According to the officer, the plan they envisioned is to accommodate more people with organised movement and vending systems, which will be beneficial to both vendors and buyers. “Even the parking charge is not expensive, as ₹15 per hour for two-wheelers and ₹30 for cars is a standard price across the city,” he explained.
The official further revealed that there are ongoing talks to redevelop the second floor of the market, which spans 9,000 sq. ft, and accommodate more shops. In addition, the market premises will also be concretised for better vending demarcations.
However, the small-time vendors point out the contrast in shifting them behind barricades for smooth vehicle movement, while barricading an actual road to facilitate access to the parking lot is itself an encroachment, they alleged.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru’s ORR companies write to GBA expressing concern over white-topping in October, WFH suggestion
briefs.deck: Pointing out that ORR supports more than 500 companies and approximately 1.3 million employees, the association argues that work-from-home (WFH) cannot be a substitute for effective infrastructure planning and traffic management.
briefs.bodyText:
The Outer Ring Road Companies Association (ORRCA) has written to the Greater Bengaluru Authority commissioner Maheshwar Rao expressing “deep disappointment and serious concern” over the move to commence white-topping work on ORR in October 2026, and government’s suggestion for “work-from-home” (WFH) to mitigate the impact.
‘Inconsistent move’
On August 4, more than 100 representatives of ORR companies had attended a meeting with senior government officials, chaired by Mr. Rao.
Nearly 70% of the participants urged the government to focus on completing the metro before launching new ORR projects. Citing delays and poor infrastructure, companies said that confidence in authorities’ execution capabilities has weakened.
According to the letter accessed by The Hindu from sources, it was agreed during the meeting that work on ORR would be consultative, technically evaluated and carefully sequenced, with the metro completion as the immediate priority.
“Against this background, the proposed commencement of major carriageway works before the metro operations and before completion of the agreed technical evaluation and stakeholder consultation appears inconsistent with the understanding reached at the Townhall,” reads the letter.
‘Work from home not a substitute for effective planning’
The letter also expresses disappointment at the State government's suggestion of work-from-home as a means of managing the resulting traffic disruption.
Pointing out that ORR supports more than 500 companies and approximately 1.3 million employees, the association argues that WFH cannot be a substitute for effective infrastructure planning and traffic management.
“This is especially concerning given the considerable effort made by ORR companies to support and secure approval for the ₹450 crore ORR Improvement Programme in January 2026. The objective was a coordinated transformation of the corridor while minimising disruption. Commencing major carriageway interventions while metro construction remains incomplete risks undermining that objective and further constraining an already stressed corridor,” the association notes in the letter.
Reiterating demands
Apart from demanding that work-from-home should not be positioned as a mitigation strategy without prior consultation with the companies, the letter also asks for white-topping/major carriageway works to be kept on hold — including tendering, award, issuance of work orders, contractor appointment, mobilisation, preparatory works and physical execution — until the agreed consultation and technical evaluation are completed.
Other demands include prioritising the metro completion and operational readiness, consultation with stakeholders regarding white-topping versus black-topping assessment before a final decision, development of a comprehensive traffic simulation, diversion and construction-management plan in consultation with ORRCA and traffic police, and an urgent meeting with ORRCA before the programme is progressed further.
Tenders soon
Acknowledging the letter, Mr. Maheshwar Rao said that they would have to devise a plan to commence the works. Whitetopping in phases is an option, he added.
A source in B-SMILE, the implementing agency, told The Hindu that they are already preparing the tender documents, which are expected to be floated in the next 15 days.
“Even the plan for the service roads has been revised, and we will use the Full Depth Reclamation (FDR) technique to lay the service roads. The estimate also has to be revised, which is currently ongoing,” he said.
This is the fourth time that the civic agency has changed the plan since the DPR was readied at the end of 2025.
It is learnt from sources that a meeting was convened at the GBA to gather opinions on the technique to be used for the ORR redevelopment, where most engineers had expressed that whitetopping was better due to its longer lifespan. However, following the meeting, many citizens had batted for blacktopping, which has now been dropped from the plans.
In addition, BTP had earlier opined that whitetopping the stretch would cause severe traffic disruption and could even lead to an acute increase in travel time for commuters.
(With inputs from Chetan B.C.)

briefs.headline: After 22 years on the run, Kerala fugitive wanted in murder cases arrested in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: Rakesh, now 49, had gone into hiding after being released on bail, following which the court declared him a proclaimed offender
briefs.bodyText:
A 49-year-old man from Kerala, who had been absconding for 22 years in multiple criminal cases, including murder and attempt to murder, has been arrested in Bengaluru by the Kannur City police.
P. Rakesh, a resident of the Thavakkara in Kannur, had been wanted in three cases registered at the Kannur Town Police station. He was an accused in the 2001 murder of one Kombra Pradeepan, the 2004 murder of one Ravindran inside the Kannur Central Jail, and an attempt to murder one Yoganandan.
Rakesh had gone into hiding after being released on bail, following which the court declared him a proclaimed offender.
Probe by special team
The arrest followed a month-long investigation by a special team formed under the direction of Kannur District Police Chief Vijay Bharath Reddy. During inquiries in Rakesh’s native place, the police learned that he had previously worked in Bengaluru. An unclear photograph obtained from an old friend of his proved crucial to the investigation. With the help of police technical experts, the photograph was enhanced and used to expand the search to Bengaluru.
The police eventually traced him living under a different identity in Tharabanahalli, near Bengaluru.
Rakesh had been living there under the name Sabu. He had married a woman from Thrissur and had been residing there with his family for around 20 years. He worked in catering and reportedly spent most of his time at home after work, leaving local residents with little information about his past.
After nearly a week of surveillance and investigation centered on Tharabanahalli, the special team identified the house where Rakesh was staying.
Around midnight on Monday (August 17, 2026), the police team surrounded the house and took him into custody. Rakesh allegedly attempted to resist the arrest by trying to use a dog kept at the house against the police. The team, however, managed to overpower him and make the arrest.

briefs.headline: SIR: With 1.10 crore voters under ASDDO, Karnataka to see one of the highest draft-stage deletions
briefs.deck: Karnataka has already crossed the highest draft-stage deletions recorded in Uttar Pradesh (19.09%) and Arunachal Pradesh (18.7%), where the exercise concluded in April
briefs.bodyText:
With more than 1.10 crore voters — one-fifth of the State’s total electoral roll — marked under the Absent, Shifted, Duplicate, Dead and Others (ASDDO) category as on August 3, Karnataka is likely to record one of the highest draft-stage electoral roll deletions in the country. The ASDDO category currently covers 19.95% of Karnataka’s voters.
Karnataka has already crossed the highest draft-stage deletions recorded in Uttar Pradesh (19.09%) and Arunachal Pradesh (18.7%), where the exercise concluded in April. In West Bengal, the rolls shrunk by 12% due to logical discrepancies, while remaining cases are still under adjudication. Even among Phase III States, Karnataka’s ASDDO is significantly higher than Haryana (16.3%) and Andhra Pradesh (10.78%).
Likely to go up further
With over 2.41 lakh enumeration forms still pending digitisation, the ASDDO figure is likely to cross 20%, as recent trends show that more than 60% of the forms digitised each day are being added to the ASDDO list.
For instance, in a day between August 1 and 2, forms ‘pending for digitisation’ reduced from 10.29 lakh to 4.89 lakh — meaning 5.40 lakh forms were digitised. During the same period, the ASDDO list increased from 1.05 crore to 1.09 crore, indicating that 4.02 lakh, or nearly 75%, of the digitised forms were marked under ASDDO.
Highest ASDDO
Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer V. Anbu Kumar admitted that the ASDDO list is intended to result in deletions, with names to be removed from the electoral roll unless voters object and establish that they are not shifted or absent.
With the August 8 deadline for enumeration approaching, the pace of digitisation has picked up sharply. However, daily data shows that of every 8-10 lakh forms digitised, more than 60% and, in recent days, as much as 75% have been marked under the ASDDO category.
The trend has remained consistent throughout the exercise. On July 22, 1.41 crore forms were pending for digitisation. By August 3, that number had fallen to 4.89 lakh, while the ASDDO list had swelled up from 24.58 lakh to 1.10 crore within 11 days.
Still have time
The CEO maintained that mahazars had been conducted in all such cases and that voters marked as absent or shifted can submit the relevant forms or get their enumeration forms corrected through the BLO until August 8. However, he did not explain where the 1.10 crore voters marked under the ASDDO category are ultimately being accounted for and due to what reasons Karnataka has bypassed other states, recording one of the highest ASDDO figures.

briefs.headline: 500 students of Clarence High School in Bengaluru fall sick, management blames street vendors
briefs.deck: As part of the Safe Footpath campaign, civic authorities promised to remove street vendors from the footpath, and ensure junk food is not sold within 50 metres radius of the school
briefs.bodyText:
After more than 500 students fell sick due to a seasonal flu-like illness and two H1N1 cases were confirmed among staff members, Clarence High School in Bengaluru was closed from August 14 to 18. Classes were shifted online.
In a letter addressed to civic authorities, Commodore Prem Reuben, Administrator, Clarence High School, stated, “There is a growing health crisis at Clarence High School, Richards Town, Bengaluru, that demands immediate intervention. More than 500 students (20% of our 2,500-strong student body) and 21 staff members are absent due to fever, cold, cough, and body ache. We have at least two confirmed cases of H1N1, and one staff member is currently undergoing treatment in Bangalore Baptist Hospital.”
Initially, the school authorities had closed the institution on August 12 as a precautionary measure. The letter stated that later, they decided to keep it closed from August 14 to 18.
What school authorities say
A representative of the Clarence High School administration told The Hindu, “As a precautionary measure, we have closed Montessori school while students of classes 1 to 5 restarted school from Tuesday (August 18). Students are getting better. Hence, offline classes are being conducted. However, for students from class 6 to 10, classes are being held online.”
Mr. Reuben, in his letter, has blamed street vendors around the school for the breakout. He also cited the condition of the surroundings of the school. “The area around the school is inevitably left dirty and unhygienic, contributing to the spread of illness and disease,” he wrote.
GBA says no link, no outbreak
However, Siddapaji Gowda, Health Officer, GBA, Bengaluru North, denied the allegations. He said, “There is no link between street vendors selling food and hundreds of children falling sick in Clarence School. It is not an outbreak, but a common cold that is contagious, airborne and spreads from one person to another. It is not because of the food outside. Probably it was not detected earlier in the school. The disease has spread among students. Only two staff members have been detected with H1N1, a strain or influenza sub-type.”
Pommala Sunil Kumar, Commissioner, Bengaluru North City Corporation, inspected the school premises. He also instructed the school management to share only responsible and verified information regarding flu infection, so as to prevent unnecessary anxiety, fear and confusion among students, parents, teachers and the general public. Active surveillance will be continued at the school for the next 15 days by GBA Health Department officials, he said.
Gurudatta Hegde, Commissioner, Health and Family Welfare Department, said, “Two staff members have tested positive for H1N1 in Clarence school. They are in the recovery stage now. There is no outbreak in the school among children. We learnt that nearly 500 students were absent, mainly due to panic. No child has tested positive for H1N1. I have instructed officials to test if any child is found symptomatic.”

stories.headline: Sustainable packaging may make food deliveries costlier by 10-30%: Zomato
stories.deck: Currently, a majority of food deliveries are done in plastic containers or plastic wrapping materials
stories.bodyText:
Use of sustainable and biodegradable packaging materials may make food orders costlier by 10% to 30% for consumers, said Anjali Ravi Kumar, Chief Sustainability Officer, Zomato Limited, a food ordering and delivery platform.
Currently, a majority of food deliveries are done in plastic containers or plastic wrapping materials and this packaging typically accounts for 5% of the total cost of the food order and is borne by the consumer.
Ms. Kumar, in a conversation with The Hindu, said the toughest challenge in replacing plastic packaging in food delivery with sustainable alternate materials such as Bagasse, aluminium, paper, and earthenware was affordability, with consumers unwilling to absorb such a premium for going green.
“Customers have to pay for the packaging, however, their willingness to pay for sustainable packaging has its limits. Sustainable packaging can become affordable as adoption increases and economies of scale kick in. Once the scale is achieved, the prices will naturally go down,’’ she elaborated.
She further said that Zomato had been encouraging packaging start-ups and restaurant partners to focus on acceptable price points and reduce costs through better manufacturing and distribution.
To take this campaign forward, Zomato has launched PackSwitch, an interactive website to help restaurants, cloud kitchens and independent food entrepreneurs find the right sustainable packaging for each item on their menu.
The platform offers information on alternative packaging materials, their functionality, business viability, and environmental impact. According to her, packaging is an important decision, especially in food deliveries, as it has to be able to handle everything from biryani to desserts while surviving the entire delivery journey. “Restaurants should plan their packaging based on their cuisine, the brand communication and the cost,’’ she added.
Zomato has introduced a low-plastic-packaging filter on its app to allow customers to identify restaurants using reduced-plastic packaging, she claimed.
Zomato’s Plastic-Free Future Programme has recognised more than 10,000 restaurants across over 500 cities for using alternatives to plastic packaging for their main menu items.

stories.headline: Tata Sons AGM put off over lack of quorum
stories.deck: Adjournment, a first in the company’s history, was due to the inability of Sir Ratan Tata Trust to nominate a member for the meeting due to regulatory curbs
stories.bodyText:
The Annual General Meeting (AGM) of Tata Sons Private Limited, the holding company of the Tata Group, which was scheduled for Tuesday (August 18, 2026), was for the first time in the company’s history adjourned due to lack of quorum, people privy to the development said.
The Tata Sons Board is expected to meet in a few weeks to decide on the next date of the AGM, the persons added. The AGM was convened at 2.30 p.m. at Bombay House, the headquarters of Tata Sons, but had to be adjourned after a half-an-hour break, as per norms. Those who attended the meeting in person included Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran, Tata Sons Board members Saurabh Agarwal and Anita M. George.
Virtual attendance
Board members Noel Tata, who is also the chairman of Tata Trusts, Venu Srinivasan and Harish Manwani attended virtually, as were other shareholders, a person privy to the meeting said. The AGM was adjourned, as Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT), the second largest shareholder in Tata Sons with 23.56%, could not nominate a member for the meeting due to an ongoing inquiry and curbs by the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner.
As per the Tata Sons Articles of Association, a jointly nominated representative of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) with a holding of 27.98% and SRTT is required for quorum. Since both the Trusts hold a 51.54% stake in Tata Sons, the legal requirement was not met.
The issue is about the composition of the trustees of SRTT and the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner, who has imposed restrictions on the trust since May 2026 after receiving complaints that three of the six trustees were lifetime or perpetual appointees.
According to Section 30A (2) of the Maharashtra Public Trusts Act, amended in September 2025, the total number of lifetime trustees must be one-fourth (25%) of the total appointees.
Since this ratio was 50% in the case of SRTT, the Charity Commissioner had ordered an inquiry. The matter is scheduled for hearing on September 8, 2026. Till that time, SRTT is barred from holding any board meetings or nominating anyone to any meeting or passing any resolution.
The AGM was to consider the financial statements of FY26, the dividend approved by the board and the reappointment of Mr. Chandrasekaran as a member of the board.
Mr. Chandrasekaran has decided to step down and not to seek reappointment at the end of his tenure in February 2027.

stories.headline: What Trump’s latest safeguard tariff move on quartz surface products means for India
stories.deck: The US accounted for 72.5% of India’s quartz surface-product exports in FY2026, according to a Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) report. India’s move does not amount to a formal WTO dispute at this stage. During the consultations, India could challenge the US assessment of increased imports and injury to domestic producers.
stories.bodyText:
India has approached the World Trade Organisation (
WTO
) over the Donald Trump administration’s move of announcing safeguard tariffs of 25% to 55% from August 15 for quartz surface products.
India approached the WTO on August 14 seeking consultations with Washington under the WTO Agreement on Safeguards. India said it had a “substantial interest” in the measure and sought access to the information provided by the US, an opportunity to discuss the safeguard action and protection of its rights under WTO rules.
It has proposed that the discussions be held virtually at a time convenient to both sides, although no date has been finalised.
India’s quartz surface products exports to the US
The US accounted for 72.5% of India’s quartz surface-product exports in FY2026, according to a Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) report. During the year, India shipped $233.3 million worth of agglomerated-quartz slabs and certain quartz and glass surface products to the US. So the industry is largely dependent on the US for exports.
Quartz surfaces are engineered stone products created by combining crushed quartz or silica with resins, pigments and other materials, followed by pressing and polishing the mixture into durable, non-porous slabs.
They are widely used for kitchen countertops, bathroom vanities, floors and wall cladding. Indian production is largely concentrated in Gujarat, Rajasthan and Telangana, with additional manufacturing capacity in Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
Among the major Indian exporters are Pokarna Engineered Stone, which markets its products under the Quantra brand, Marudhar Quartz Surfaces, KalingaStone-linked companies, ARO Granite Industries, Pacific Quartz Surfaces, Camrola Quartz, Esprit Stones, Mahi Granites, Keros Stone and Quartzkraft, the GTRI report said.
“Indian manufacturers have designed their slab sizes, patterns, certifications and distribution networks for the large US countertop and home-renovation market, making it difficult to shift quickly to other markets,” GTRI notes.
India has initiated consultations at the WTO
India’s exports of quartz surface products to the US, valued at $233.3 million, will face safeguard tariffs ranging from 25% to 55% from August 15. These products, commonly used for kitchen countertops, bathroom walls and flooring, are manufactured primarily in Gujarat, Rajasthan and Telangana.
India’s move does not amount to a formal WTO dispute at this stage. During the consultations, India could challenge the US assessment of increased imports and injury to domestic producers, while also seeking an exemption, a dedicated quota or modifications to the safeguard measures.
The US safeguard will remain in force for four years, from August 15, 2026, through August 14, 2030. During the first year, a global quota of 13.006 million square metres will apply, with the permitted volume divided into four quarterly allocations. India has not been assigned a specific quota and will therefore have to compete with other countries covered by the measure for access to the US market.
Imports falling within the quota will attract an additional 25% duty, while shipments exceeding the quota will face a 50% tariff.
Quartz countertop slabs that were previously allowed to enter the US duty-free will consequently face tariffs ranging from 25% to 50%. For covered glass products, which already carry a 5% tariff, the overall duty burden will rise to between 30% and 55%. Antidumping and countervailing duties could be imposed in addition to these tariffs.
Canada, Mexico, Australia, South Korea, Singapore and several other US free-trade partners, along with certain small developing-country suppliers, have been excluded from the safeguard. India and China, however, remain subject to the measure.
What it means
A large portion of Indian exports of these products already attract antidumping and countervailing duties in the US, says GTRI founder Ajay Srivastava. Pokarna, Marudhar and 44 other Indian companies that have undergone review currently have a zero antidumping rate, while suppliers that have not been reviewed generally face a 1.02% rate. Countervailing duties range between 1.57% and 2.34%, with an “all others” rate of 2.17%.
Antique Marbonite is an outlier, having received an antidumping margin of 323.12% in an earlier review after the US Commerce Department applied “adverse facts available.”
The newly imposed safeguard duties will come on top of these existing company-specific duties.
“India may question whether the US established increased imports, serious injury and a clear causal link under WTO rules. It may also challenge the representative period, quota size, absence of an India-specific allocation, cumulative duties and different treatment of excluded suppliers. India’s immediate objective may be an exclusion or negotiated country arrangement, alongside transparent quota administration,” says Ajay Srivastava.
“Indian producers may also accelerate diversification into Europe and the Gulf, develop lower-silica surfaces and expand domestic demand. If consultations fail, India has preserved its right to pursue further WTO action,” he adds.
The episode also offers a broader lesson: when more than 70% of an industry’s exports depend on one market, even a single trade measure can cause lasting damage.
“Indian producers may therefore need to diversify into Europe, the Gulf and other markets, develop lower-silica products and expand domestic demand, while the government builds an early-warning system to respond to foreign trade-remedy investigations before decisions are finalised,” GTRI concludes.

stories.headline: US-Canada tariff clock ticks: Last-minute talks to avert Trump’s 50% tariffs
stories.deck: The race against time for a tariff agreement unfolds between the United States and Canada, as President Trump has set a firm deadline, warning of hefty tariffs on Canadian imports. With negotiations proving to be both intense and fragile, both nations are eager to find common ground before the clock runs out, especially given the economic implications of renewed tariffs amidst ongoing trade…
stories.bodyText:
The United States and Canada are in a race against the clock to reach a tariff agreement before a 12:01 am Wednesday deadline imposed by US President Donald Trump.
Failure to strike a deal could see Trump impose 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian products, including everything from hockey sticks to tongue depressors.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney confirmed that the talks were underway earlier on Monday, but gave little away about the negotiations.
″We are negotiating,” Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney told reporters Monday, speaking in French. “The negotiations are very intense and delicate. This is not the time to talk about negotiations in public.”
Carney and Trump also spoke by phone Monday afternoon about the trade negotiations, according to Carney's office, as both sides sought to make progress before the deadline.
Old trade disputes, new tensions
Trade disagreements between the US and Canada are not new. The neighbours have sparred for years over issues including Canadian softwood lumber exports and US demands for greater access to Canada's protected dairy market.
Yet those disputes have not stopped the two countries from maintaining a close relationship as allies, friends and major trading partners. Canadian troops fought alongside US forces in Afghanistan after 9/11, while their 5,525-mile border remains undefended.
The scale of their economic and human ties is equally significant. Nearly 330,000 people and $2 billion worth of goods cross the border every day, while about 800,000 Canadians live in the United States.
Trump's stance on Canada has nevertheless shaken that traditionally cooperative relationship. His administration has imposed tariffs on Canadian goods as part of an effort to bring manufacturing back to the United States. Trump has also repeatedly spoken about making Canada America's 51st state.
The rhetoric and tariff measures have fuelled anger in Canada. A petition seeking the expulsion of US ambassador Pete Hoekstra, a Trump ally, had gathered nearly 218,000 signatures since July 21. It accuses Hoekstra of having “normalized’’ Trump's talk of annexing Canada, among other things.
Both sides have reasons to step back
Canada has a major economic stake in the outcome of the negotiations. Nearly 72% of the country's goods exports last year went to the United States.
Washington, too, faces potential costs from another round of tariffs. The importers who pay the tariffs may try to pass those costs on to consumers through higher prices, at a time when American voters are already unhappy about the cost of living. The new tariffs would also come ahead of November's midterm elections.
“I don’t think either side really wants these tariffs to come into effect,’’ said Ryan Majerus, a partner at King & Spalding and a former US trade official. “There’s a pretty strong push on both sides to find an off ramp here.’’
Majerus said Washington wants Canada to purchase more US military equipment, including F-35 fighters, participate in Trump's “Golden Dome’’ missile defence system and provide the United States with greater access to critical minerals. The aim would be to reduce America's reliance on supplies from China.
Ottawa, meanwhile, wants the US to ease tariffs on steel and aluminium and softwood lumber. The United States has argued that Canadian softwood lumber receives unfair government subsidies.
Trump uses a century-old tariff weapon
The latest dispute comes as tariffs remain central to Trump's second-term economic policy.
Last year, Trump imposed double-digit import taxes on almost every country, citing the longstanding US trade deficit as a national emergency. The Supreme Court ruled in February that he had exceeded his authority, striking down those tariffs and paving the way for the federal government to issue refunds to importers.
Trump subsequently looked for alternative ways to impose tariffs. Last month, his administration introduced import taxes of 10% to 12.5% on 59 countries and the European Union, which together account for 99% of US imports. The move was justified on the grounds that those countries allegedly failed to have or enforce restrictions on imports produced using forced labour.
For Canada, Trump has reached further back, invoking Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to impose 50% tariffs on goods representing about 5% of Canadian exports to the US.
Section 338 has never been used before. US trade officials have traditionally relied instead on Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which Trump used for last month's forced-labour tariffs.
The 1930 provision allows the president to impose tariffs of up to 50% on imports from countries that have discriminated against US businesses. It does not require an investigation and does not set a limit on how long the tariffs can remain in place.
Trump has accused Canada of discriminating against US exports of autos, alcohol and cheese. He has also singled out Canada and China because they were the only countries to respond with retaliatory tariffs after he imposed levies on their goods last year.
“If a country retaliates against us, we’re obviously not going to tolerate that,” U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told reporters Friday at the Iowa State Fair. “We’ll take action. My sense is the Canadians, they want to have a more conciliatory approach, but we’ll see.”
The tariff standoff is unfolding alongside negotiations over the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement, the North American trade pact that Trump pressured Canada and Mexico to accept during his first term.

briefs.headline: India's economic growth to slow to 6.8% FY27 amid West Asia crisis, El Nino impact
briefs.deck: Earlier this month, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had raised growth projections from 6.6% to 6.7% citing resilient domestic economy.
briefs.bodyText:
India Ratings & Research on Tuesday (August 18, 2026) projected India's GDP growth to slow down to 6.8% in the current fiscal year, as against 7.6% in the previous year, citing risks from fuel and food inflation stemming from West Asia conflict's uncertainty, weak currency, and the likely impact of El Niño on agriculture.
The FY27 GDP growth projection at 6.8 per cent is a tad higher than the 6.7% growth Ind-Ra had projected in May.
Earlier this month, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had raised growth projections from 6.6% to 6.7% citing resilient domestic economy.
The domestic rating agency said it now estimates the average crude oil price at $85 per barrel in FY27, compared to $95 per barrel in May 2026. It expects the rupee-dollar exchange rate to average ₹93.98 (May 2026: ₹94.28), a depreciation of 6.4% YoY, in FY27.
Fitch Group subsidiary Ind-Ra estimates capital flows of $70 billion under foreign currency non-resident (bank) (FCNR B) and external commercial borrowings (ECBs).
The slowdown in GDP growth in FY27 vis-a-vis FY26 is attributed to higher fuel and food inflation stemming from the West Asia conflict's uncertainty, weak currency, and the likely impact of El Niño on agriculture, Ind-Ra said in a statement.
The agency has forecast quarterly GDP growth at 6.9, 6.6, 6.7, and 6.9% for April-June, July-September, October-December, and January-March as against the RBI's prediction of 7, 6.4, 6.5, and 6.8, respectively.
Ind-Ra Chief Economist and Head — Public Finance Devendra Pant said the crude oil price of the Indian basket averaged $101.31 per barrel in the June quarter of FY27 and $96.49 per barrel for April-July 2026.
"Our crude oil price assumption for FY27 is USD85/bbl. Lower oil prices positively impact the Indian economy by reducing the trade/current account deficit (CAD). However, higher inflation due to El Niño may limit growth upside from lower oil prices," Mr. Pant said.
Ind-Ra estimates retail inflation to average 4.9% in the current fiscal year, compared to 2% in FY26. The current account deficit is estimated to rise to 1.5% of GDP, from 0.6% in FY26.
The FY27 deficit target of 4.3% remains challenging due to subsidies on liquefied petroleum gas and fertilisers. While direct tax collection and non-tax revenue may support achieving the fiscal deficit target, indirect tax collection may pose challenging, Mr. Pant said.

briefs.headline: Government to allocate additional 200 SCM gas in latest push for domestic PNG
briefs.deck: The objective here is to help CGDs offset their LNG-sourcing costs which have stayed elevated as episodic tensions continue to mar supplies from West Asia.
briefs.bodyText:
Seeking to further fuel its push for adoption of piped natural gas (PNG), the government on Tuesday (August 18, 2026) evening announced eligible city-gas distributors (CGDs) would be allocated an additional 200 standard cubic metres (SCM) of the lower-priced Administered Price Mechanism (APM) natural gas for every incremental billed domestic-PNG connection they scale, effective September 1.
Further, the government informed that this would be “over and above” the threshold level determined for the respective geographical area.
The objective here is to help CGDs offset their LNG-sourcing costs – by allocating additional APM gas – centred on accelerating domestic PNG connections. At present, the price of LNG continues to stay elevated because of the episodic tensions in West Asia.
The natural gas produced by India’s upstream majors, OIL and ONGC, from their conventional fields is referred to as APM gas.
The incentivising mechanism would be implemented over two tranches spanning six months.
“The resulting cost savings are expected to shorten the payback period for capital expenditure incurred on D-PNG connections from around 10 years to approximately 3 years — giving CGD entities a strong financial incentive to expand household PNG connectivity more rapidly, bringing the benefits of clean, safe and affordable piped cooking gas to a larger number of Indian households in the months ahead,” read the government statement.

briefs.headline: Meta trial that could reshape Facebook, Instagram gets underway
briefs.deck: Meta founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg is expected to testify during the multi-week trial, as is Instagram head Adam Mosseri
briefs.bodyText:
A coalition of States suing Meta Platforms over claims Facebook and Instagram were designed in ways that harmed young users’ mental health will begin making its case on Tuesday in California at a federal court in a trial that could reshape some of the most popular apps on the planet.
Attorneys for Colorado, California, New Jersey and Kentucky, who are leading a bipartisan group of 29 states, will give their opening statements before an eight-person jury in Oakland that is serving expressly in an advisory capacity for U.S. District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers, who will ultimately decide the case.
The trial will test the four States’ allegations that Meta designed Facebook and Instagram to be addictive to children and teens and misled consumers about the safety of the platforms for young users. It will also address the claims of all 29 States accusing Meta of improperly collecting and using children’s personal data while they used the firm’s platforms in violation of federal law.
Attorneys for Meta are expected to tell the jury that the company has made a huge effort to keep kids safe online. The company has argued that it has not made misleading statements about safety and the States have failed to present any evidence of actual harm to their residents.
Meta founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg is expected to testify during the multi-week trial, as is Instagram head Adam Mosseri.
Biggest test yet
In terms of potential damages and implications for Meta, experts have said the trial is the biggest test yet of youth social media litigation and comes amid a broader reckoning across the globe over social media’s effects on young users. Meta has said the penalties could be as high as $1.4 trillion, near the company’s market cap of $1.5 trillion.

briefs.headline: India’s crude import bill surges 41% in July amid West Asia crisis; volumes up 13%
briefs.deck: Episodic events in West Asia had kept prices on benchmark brent crude largely volatile in July this year.
briefs.bodyText:
i
India’s crude oil import bill surged more than 41% year-on-year to $13.7 billion in July, according to provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), as elevated global oil prices amid persistent uncertainty in West Asia pushed up the cost of shipments.
The country’s crude oil imports rose 13.3% in volume terms to 21.4 million metric tonnes (MMT) in July, compared with 18.9 MMT in the same month last year. However, the sharp increase in international crude prices resulted in a significantly higher import outgo.
India’s crude basket averaged $82.04 a barrel in July, up from $70.95 a barrel a year earlier. Benchmark Brent crude prices remained volatile during the month as episodic developments in West Asia continued to influence market sentiment.
Brent crude futures were trading more than 1% higher at around $91.84 a barrel on Tuesday evening following the latest escalation in the region.
LNG imports remain largely stable
India’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports increased marginally by 1.5% year-on-year to 2,915 million standard cubic metres (MMSCM) in July.
India remains heavily dependent on overseas supplies to meet its energy requirements, with crude oil imports accounting for 88.5% of the country’s total crude oil consumption, according to the provisional PPAC data.
Petroleum product exports rise
Meanwhile, exports of petroleum products by Indian oil-marketing companies increased 10% year-on-year to 5.5 MMT in July.
Revenue from petroleum product exports rose to $5 billion during the month, compared with $3.3 billion a year earlier.
Overall, the country’s net import bill for oil and gas – which is the difference between petroleum products, crude and gas imports; and exports of petroleum products – increased more than 19% on a year-over-year basis to $11.2 billion.

briefs.headline: Skoda Auto Volkswagen Group focuses on product intervention, localisation to grow market share in India, ready for higher ethanol blends
briefs.bodyText:
European car maker, the Volkswagen Group, having six brands in the Indian market which includes Škoda, Volkswagen, Audi, Porshe, Bentley and Lamborghini, will be focusing on enhancing its product portfolio and growing localisation to drive growth in the future.
Describing India as an “extremely important and strategic market” for the automobile Group, Piyush Arora Managing Director & CEO, Skoda Auto Volkswagen Group India in an interview said product intervention and tapping into Indian engineering talent to develop future software-defined vehicles and connectivity will remain key to the Group’s India strategy.
“We have seen a good amount of growth momentum in the passenger vehicle space, but the market is being driven highly by product intervention,” he said ahead of the launch of the new Slavia sedan by Škoda Auto India.
Stating that the Group would introduce new products across brands, he said last year the it had launched Octavia RS, Golf GT, Tiguan RS.
Under Audi it will bring in the new Q3 which will be launched towards the end of this year. “The A5 is coming in and also we are looking at introducing the flagship Audi the Q9 which we want to bring into the country,” Mr Arora said.
He said Bentley and Porsche are doing “extremely well” in terms of their segment and last year the Group sold 113 units of Lamborghinis.
“We are looking product interventions at every brand. This very clearly shows the commitment of the Volkswagen Group to the market in India and as we go along, we will bring the right product at the right time,” he stated.
Stating that the tariff challenges for the group for the U.S. market are substantial, he said the limited growth happening in European market and the transformation happening towards electrification as well as competitive pressure in the Chinese market has put India at the “bright spot” for the Group.
“That’s how our group looks at it and all the brands look at it, so we are extremely committed and we also see great opportunity in India,” Mr. Arora emphasized.
He said though the India-UK FTA will benefit the Bentley brand, the upcoming India-EU bilateral trade agreement will provide further opportunity across its brands.
“We are looking at growth in India. We have grown almost 7 to 8 percent for Škoda brand in the first half of this year. We hope to continue that momentum. The market has grown also in the alternate power trains this year, so you see substantial growth happening in the CNG space and growth happening in electric vehicle space where we do not have product offering at this point in time,” Mr Arora said.
He said considering the growth in India and the way the product and the market is evolving, the Group will evaluate the product portfolio offering and the gaps in its portfolio.
“We are evaluating alternate power trains whether it is electrification or offering a CNG product and we will bring in the products,” he stated.
On the E20 issue he said all the company’s products have been developed for E20 compliance compatibility as well as compliance since 2020 and they can handle higher level of blending.
“The product which we are selling in the market is fully compliant with the E20 and being an engineering driven company, we always have certain safety margins in our design and development which we built in,” he said.
“And I can also mention that compatibility wise, our product can even take a little bit higher percentage of ethanol blending. So, maybe while there are tests which might be conducted for any higher grade of ethanol blending say E25, I can say that compatibility wise product will meet that requirement,” he emphasized.
“We always advise our customers to fill the fuel in the authorised fuel station where the chances of alterations are less and if there are alteration driven challenges faced by some customers, the oil marketing companies are addressing that,” he said.
Heb said the Group was bringing a lot of product interventions.
“We are very hopeful that we will be able to participate in the growth which we are expecting in the festive season,” he added.

stories.headline: What is Jamal Musiala suffering from? ‘Absence seizures’ explained
stories.deck: Jamal Musiala has revealed he has been diagnosed with brief absence seizures, caused by temporary abnormal brain activity. The episodes led to collapses during two Bayern Munich friendlies but are treatable and being managed by specialists. Musiala says he feels well, has medical clearance to continue football, remains optimistic and asks for privacy regarding further details.
stories.bodyText:
Jamal Musiala has revealed that he has been diagnosed with “temporarily occurring, brief absence seizures” after collapsing during two Bayern Munich friendlies within four days. The 23-year-old Germany international said the episodes are caused by a neurological dysfunction, are treatable and are currently being managed with specialist medical care.
The disclosure came after Musiala collapsed during Tuesday’s 4-2 friendly win over Heidenheim, just days after a similar episode against RB Leipzig. He has since said that he is doing well, remains optimistic and, after consultation with neurological specialists, intends to continue living normally and pursuing his career in football.
What are absence seizures?
Absence seizures involve brief, sudden lapses in consciousness. They are much more common in children than adults and can sometimes be mistaken for a person simply losing concentration or staring into space.
According to the 
Mayo Clinic
, a simple absence seizure typically lasts about 10 seconds, although it can last as long as 30 seconds. During an episode, the person may suddenly stop what they are doing and stare blankly into space before quickly returning to an alert state.
Massachusetts General Hospital describes
 the loss of awareness as usually lasting between five and 30 seconds. A person experiencing one may appear to be daydreaming and may not respond normally to what is happening around them.
There is generally no confusion, headache or drowsiness after a typical absence seizure, and the person may have no memory of the episode. If episodes happen repeatedly, however, they can interfere with everyday activities. Small movements such as eyelid fluttering, lip smacking, chewing motions or finger rubbing can also occur, according to the Mayo Clinic and Massachusetts General Hospital.
A typical absence seizure does not usually involve the dramatic muscle jerking associated with some other seizure types, and people generally recover quickly without the confusion, headache or drowsiness that can follow other seizures.
That distinction matters when considering what has been seen with Musiala. The Bayern midfielder has appeared disoriented and collapsed during matches, but his public statement does not provide enough medical detail to determine precisely how his individual episodes present beyond the diagnosis he disclosed.
Why can someone appear to collapse during an episode?
An absence seizure is fundamentally a temporary interruption of awareness rather than the kind of prolonged loss of consciousness that people may associate with a conventional faint.
That distinction is relevant to what happened with Musiala. During both Bayern matches, he appeared disoriented before going down, with the incidents occurring while he was actively playing.
Against RB Leipzig on Saturday, August 15, Musiala appeared unsteady before beginning to fall. New Bayern team-mate Ismael Saibari reacted immediately, catching him and helping lower him safely to the ground before medical staff attended to him.
Musiala was able to leave the pitch under his own power and subsequently returned to training.
Four days later, he came off the bench against Heidenheim and suffered another episode. Players from both teams surrounded him as medical staff came onto the pitch, before he was helped away from the playing area.
The repeated nature of the incidents prompted understandable concern, but Musiala subsequently explained that both episodes were connected to the diagnosis he had received.
What causes absence seizures?
Absence seizures occur because of abnormal electrical activity in the brain, temporarily disrupting normal awareness.
The condition is particularly associated with childhood. The Mayo Clinic says absence seizures are more common in children, while Massachusetts General Hospital notes that they can begin in childhood, most commonly between the ages of 8 and 15, although some people continue experiencing them into adulthood.
Some episodes can also be triggered by factors such as flashing lights or rapid, deep breathing, according to the medical information provided by Massachusetts General Hospital.
There is no information from Musiala indicating what specifically triggered either of his recent episodes, and he has asked for the details of his condition to remain private.
How concerning is it for Musiala to have an episode while playing football?
An absence seizure itself is generally brief and does not usually cause physical injury. The Mayo Clinic notes, however, that the circumstances in which one occurs can create risks. A sudden lapse in awareness while driving, cycling or performing another activity where continuous attention is required can result in injury.
For an elite footballer, the question is therefore not simply whether an absence seizure is usually physically damaging. A temporary loss of awareness while running, challenging for the ball or moving at speed can create an entirely different set of risks.
Musiala has specifically addressed that concern himself. He said that, in his case, “there is no additional health risk beyond this” and that, after consultation with neurological specialists, he had been cleared to continue his normal life and pursue football.
He also said he was receiving the best possible medical care and remained “very optimistic,” according to his statement.
What happened to Musiala before this?
The latest diagnosis comes after several difficult seasons from an injury perspective.
Musiala suffered a serious ankle injury during the 2025 FIFA Club World Cup following a challenge involving then-Paris Saint-Germain goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma. The injury kept him out for several months, with his return coming in the second half of the following season.
He subsequently dealt with further ankle problems that disrupted his recovery and limited his ability to regain his best form. He nevertheless returned to the Germany squad for the 2026 World Cup and started three of the country's four matches at the tournament.
The two recent Bayern incidents are therefore separate from that injury history and concern a neurological condition that Musiala has only now publicly identified.
What has Musiala said about his future?
Musiala also sought to reassure supporters about what comes next, saying he remains optimistic about his recovery and feels well supported by Bayern Munich and those around him. “I know they might look scary at first glance, but for me, they are currently just part of my everyday life,” he wrote, adding that he was “receiving excellent medical care” and that “FC Bayern and my personal support network are right by my side, helping me through this.”
With clearance from his neurological specialists, Musiala said it was his own decision to continue with his normal life and return to the activity that matters most to him. “With the medical clearance of the neurologists, I want to continue doing what helps my recovery the most: simply living my daily life and pursuing my passion for playing football,” he said.
He added that he had taken responsibility for the decision and was feeling positive about his progress. “Overall, I feel very positive and am on the right track,” Musiala wrote, before turning his attention towards Bayern’s season and the possibility of continuing to compete for trophies with his team.
“What helps me most on this journey is continuing to chase victories and titles with my team and with your amazing support,” he said.
Musiala also asked supporters to respect his wish to keep the details of his condition private, limiting those discussions to his closest circle, the club and his medical experts.

stories.headline: A unique experience awaits athletes at the Asian Games
